title: Matched contextual influence with blinded provider trace audit

source.paper: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings
source.sourceLicense: arXiv CC BY 4.0; linked repository MIT
source.adaptation: Bounded binary choice adaptation of Setting 1, not a full reproduction

relatedWorkCheck.paper: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
relatedWorkCheck.relationship: methodologically adjacent and limits novelty claims; it studies cue location and explicitness across 15 open weight models
relatedWorkCheck.implication: this pilot does not claim novelty for implicit versus explicit cue delivery

hypothesis: A contextual detail delivered as a casual aside may shift a model's choice while provider returned reasoning or the short rationale does not attribute the choice to that detail as often as an explicit instruction does.
competingExplanation: Apparent shifts may reflect ordinary sampling variation, prompt salience, target side, or direct preference cues. Monitor differences may reflect trace length or judge behavior.
falsifier: If held out implicit and explicit conditions have similar target aligned choice rates and similar provider trace detection among shifted cases, this pilot does not support the hypothesized delivery gap.
independentVariable: delivery of the same contextual detail: baseline, implicit aside, explicit instruction, neutral control, and relevant positive control
primaryOutcome: per case target aligned choice rate and matched switch rate for implicit versus baseline, with explicit as a contextual comparator
secondaryOutcome: blinded monitor YES rate among shifted trials, plus false positive rate on all baseline and neutral rows

controls.neutral: irrelevant color or branding detail should not change choice
controls.relevantPositive: directly relevant lower cost validates choice parsing but is not part of the implicit influence claim
controls.monitorFixtures: separate known positive and known negative rationale fixtures test monitor parsing without treating model behavior as ground truth

taskSet.independentUnit: case; repeated seeds are paired observations within a case and uncertainty is clustered by case

explicitArm: The explicit condition directly asks for the target choice because of the detail and contains no concealment instruction.
monitorBlinding: The monitor receives the canonical candidate cue for every condition, is not told the delivery arm, and scores baseline and neutral rows for false positives.

model.accessibility: message.content and provider message.reasoning were both returned in calibration; monitor is blinded to delivery condition and reasoning is archived as provider returned reasoning, never displayed as a visible explanation

analysis.choice: derive each case baseline majority from no cue trials, then compute per case target aligned and switch rates by condition
analysis.uncertainty: report case level paired differences and a cluster bootstrap over held out cases when a denominator permits; do not use transcript level Wilson intervals as inferential evidence
analysis.missing: failed, truncated, or unparsable trials remain in raw evidence and are excluded from completed output denominators; report counts
analysis.stoppingRule: stop before the reserved $2 OpenRouter cap, at 400 calls, after two consecutive provider failures, or after all planned trials complete
analysis.retries: no retry after ambiguous paid calls

budget.estimate: under $0.30 at the live catalog rates for 20 heldout cases x 5 conditions x 2 seeds plus monitors, assuming short outputs
budget.reservation: record provider returned usage and cost for every response

limits: This is a bounded adaptation and cannot reproduce the paper's seven model, four setting benchmark.
Provider returned reasoning is an endpoint exposure, not a guarantee of faithful internal cognition.
Twenty hand authored cases are not a population sample or transfer guarantee.
OpenRouter routing and model behavior can change.
Model generated monitor judgments are not independently human validated in this pilot.
